body:
**Credit name.** Evan Daniel (GitHub @evand).

**Claim.** One new upper bound.  The side is the certificate's exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places.

| n | New upper bound | Best public before it | Improvement | That bound's source |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 183 | 13.999580178737 | 14 | 4.20e-4 | the 14 × 14 grid |

As far as we know this is the first packing of 183 squares below side 14.  In k² − c terms: 183 = 14² − 13, so the
k = 14 row now reaches c = 13 (182 = 14² − 14 was the last sub-grid count before).

Comparison = the lowest of the register (main @804eff36, its witness and case page), open and closed issues through
#678, David Ellsworth's catalogue, and every value those give through the monotone envelope.  Checked 18 October.

**Certificate.** In https://github.com/evand/square-packing at commit
[3a9948c](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/tree/3a9948c/search/packer/candidates):
`s183_h183b.cert` (the certificate), `s183_h183b.exact.txt` (the 80-digit KKT point), `s183_h183b.input.txt` (the
f64 packing it was solved from), `s183_h183b.json` (the solver's report), and `s183_h183b_regularized.cert` (the same
packing at the same side, regularized for display: 18 angle groups).  Same format as #659, #664 and #669.

| file | S' (certificate side) | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `s183_h183b.cert` | 13.999580178736252502081470897571 | 279e70d1c7fb0bc181e3e9d313e7350b672d85e223296f252b92f2916d6e5df5 |
| `s183_h183b_regularized.cert` | 13.999580178736252502081470897571 | 67b2b26205f53915bb1a10a703a2700994a9ad16ea9ddd427bda232716f40d58 |

**Checking.**  `search/exact/verify_cert.py` (separating axes) and `search/exact/verify_cert2.py` (polygon
intersection) both accept both files; exact rational, standard library only:
`python3 search/exact/verify_cert.py search/packer/candidates/s183_h183b.cert`.  They share an author (us) and the
certificate format; the geometry tests differ.

**Local optimality** (numerical evidence at 80 digits, not interval proofs): exact side S* =
13.999580178736252501941…; KKT point, local minimum of the side, strict modulo 27 exact flat motions; no
corner–corner MILP descent; 86 wall + 897 square–square contact equations, 106 corner–corner contacts; 1 rattler;
73 tilted squares (72 load-bearing) in two bands: 22 down the upper left at 23.4°–29.5°, and 51 in a 5-row band
across the bottom, mostly at 18.1°–19.7°.  The same two-band family as the s(156), s(182) and s(211) records.

**How it was found (lineage).**  Please credit Francisco Couzo's s(182) packing (the register's witness, 13.974090713)
as the ultimate start.
1. **182 donor.**  Our basin explorer (`search/packer/explore.py`: fixed-side perturbation moves + re-polish), run at
   n = 182 on 17 October from Couzo's witness, produced a non-record 182 packing at 13.990326 after 17 moves.
2. **Insertion.**  On 18 October we inserted one square into each of ~120 distinct sub-14 182 packings from our
   store (`search/packer/h183.py`: dilate the packing 0.2–1.2 %, put the new square in one of the 12 largest holes,
   quench).  Over 90 % of these collapse to the grid; the one from that donor quenched to 14.0335 with no full axis
   line.
3. **Explorer at 183** (40 minutes, from that seed and five similar ones, all descended from public 182 packings):
   one tilt-angle swap, then two two-parent crossovers (the second parent is another packing from the same run; the
   run didn't log which), reaching 13.9998051 (certified: S* = 13.9998051157950716…).
4. **Refinement:** twelve 40-minute explorer runs from that packing; all twelve reached this one, by three symmetric
   kicks plus re-polishing.  `exactsolve.py` then certified it.

Insertion into the 182 record itself (120 seeds, four explorer runs) never got below 14.0135; the non-record donors
did better.
title: s(183) ≤ 13.999580178737: registration request (first 183 below the grid)
